  • Architecture & Scoping: Partner with account teams to discover client requirements, design scalable OpenBao/Vault solutions, draft technical proposals, and define statements of work (SOWs).
  • Proof-of-Concept (PoC) Leadership: Lead technical demonstrations, PoCs, and architectural evaluations to showcase value and overcome technical objections to close deals.
  • Global Collaboration: Work closely with our distributed global team to align pre-sales solution designs with delivery capabilities and ensure seamless project handovers.

Technical Delivery & Consulting

  • Secrets Management Architecture: Architect, deploy, and harden enterprise-grade OpenBao instances running across cloud-native and on-premises environments.
  • Migrations & Upgrades: Advise and execute seamless migration paths from proprietary or legacy secrets management systems to OpenBao.

Community & Thought Leadership

  • Contribute to open-source tools, upstream OpenBao initiatives, and internal ControlPlane security research.
  • Represent ControlPlane at technical conferences, webinars, and community meetups.

What We’re Looking For

Core Secrets Management Expertise

  • Deep, practical experience with either OpenBao or HashiCorp Vault (architectural design, high availability, dynamic secrets, PKI, auto-unseal mechanisms, namespace/policy design, and identity engines).
  • Hands-on experience with secrets migration, lifecycle management, and disaster recovery strategies.

Pre-Sales & Client-Facing Skills

  • Proven track record in a technical pre-sales, solution architecture, or customer-facing consulting role.
  • Strong ability to translate complex security and compliance concepts into business value for C-level executives, security leadership, and platform engineers.
  • Confident presentation skills with a demonstrated ability to guide clients through complex sales cycles and build technical trust.

Cloud-Native & DevSecOps Engineering

  • Experience with cloud-native architectures and container orchestration platforms (Kubernetes, EKS, GKE, AKS, or OpenShift).
  • Strong knowledge of Infrastructure as Code using Terraform or OpenTofu.
  • Familiarity with CI/CD security automation and pipeline hardening.
  • Working knowledge or desire to code/script in Golang, Python, or CLI tooling.

Location & Eligibility

  • Must be located in the UK or Europe with existing right to work (remote or hybrid London).
  • Ability to align work hours with European client time zones while collaborating with a global team.

Benefits

ControlPlane is a dynamic, cutting-edge and passionate business to work for. Our employees are at the heart of our business, which means we care about our culture, our people and their progression.

Alongside this, as a colleague you will have the following benefits:

  • Generous and competitive salary + Bonus
  • 33 days of paid holiday, including paid leave for the standard 8 UK Bank Holidays
  • Enhanced Parental Leave
  • Private Medical and Dental Insurance
  • An individual training budget for personal development, including but not limited to:
    • Conferences
    • Training (books, courses, coaching, as well as internal training which is of course included beyond budget)
    • Qualifications

We believe our peers are equally as important as the technology we use. We’re looking for people of the highest personal calibre: quietly confident, with a strong work ethic, keenness to learn, emotional maturity and respect, who understand that “we” is more than “me” and who embrace human diversity of all kinds.

As we grow, you’ll help us build a company culture of which we can all be proud. If you share these values, we want to hear from you!

raw.description:
ICS.AI · Remote (UK), occasional travel to Basingstoke and client sites

Full-time, permanent

Up to £45,000

Keep the roadmap clear, the backlogs ready and AI product delivery moving.

ICS.AI is a UK AI consultancy delivering AI transformation to the public sector, local government, higher education and the wider public estate. Our SMART AI products help organisations improve resident and staff experiences through conversational AI, copilots, automation and intelligent insights.

We are hiring a Product Manager to sit at the operational centre of our product function. You will maintain the combined roadmap and backlogs across the SMART AI product range, turn agreed priorities into well-organised and scheduled work, and keep Product, Delivery and Engineering aligned from refinement through to release.

This is a hands-on coordination and delivery role for someone who enjoys bringing structure to competing priorities. You will not need to own every product decision yourself; you will make sure agreed decisions are translated into clear, buildable work and carried through consistently across products and teams.

What you’ll be doing

  • Maintaining the combined roadmap across SMART AI products and keeping product backlogs ordered against agreed priorities.
  • Facilitating cross-product backlog refinement and sprint planning with Product Specialists.
  • Preparing prioritisation recommendations and carrying agreed decisions through into scheduled work.
  • Checking that work items are complete, estimated and ready before they enter a sprint.
  • Coordinating between Product, Delivery and Engineering, tracking progress and keeping priorities and status aligned.
  • Maintaining and sequencing engineering work queues, with clear visibility of capacity, dependencies and work in progress.
  • Maintaining the shared platform backlog and tracking dependencies between the platform and the products built on it.
  • Coordinating client UAT and tracking work through to release.
  • Producing clear roadmap, progress, queue-status and backlog-health reporting.

What makes this role different

You will work across a connected family of AI products rather than managing a single isolated backlog. The role combines product operations, delivery coordination and practical judgement about GenAI and agentic AI. Your impact will be visible in the quality of the work entering delivery, the flow of work across teams and the clarity of the roadmap for the wider business.

What we’re looking for

We are not screening on a specific degree or qualification. We care about evidence that you can bring structure, judgement and momentum to product delivery:

  • Experience maintaining a product backlog or roadmap in a Product Manager, Product Owner, Business Analyst or similar delivery role within technology, AI or software.
  • A structured and organised approach to competing requests across several products or teams.
  • Confidence working with product, client-facing, delivery and engineering colleagues, including facilitating planning and refinement sessions.
  • Strong attention to detail when reviewing work items, acceptance criteria, estimates and dependencies.
  • A practical understanding of how software is designed, built and released.
  • Working knowledge of GenAI, large language models and agentic AI, sufficient to discuss feasibility and sequencing.
  • Clear written communication and disciplined decision recording.
  • Eligibility to work in the UK. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Nice to have

  • Experience with Azure DevOps Boards, delivery plans or equivalent tooling.
  • Experience with Scrum, Kanban or flow-based work management.
  • Exposure to AI-assisted or agentic software delivery.
  • Experience of SaaS products, cloud platforms or shared platform dependencies.
  • Experience of local government or wider public sector service delivery.

Qualifications and development

Formal qualifications are not required. We support relevant professional development and qualifications that help you grow in the role.

The package

  • Salary up to £45,000.
  • Full-time, permanent role.
  • Remote within the UK, with occasional travel to Basingstoke and client sites.
  • £100 per month working-from-home allowance.
  • Vitality Healthcare Plan.
  • Pension scheme.
  • 25 days’ holiday.
  • Support for relevant professional development and qualifications.

Ready to help shape how AI products move from priority to delivery?

Apply to join ICS.AI and help us keep an ambitious product portfolio clear, coordinated and moving.

Salary: up to £45K

raw.description:
About the Role

Shields Facilities Management (SFM) is seeking a strategic, detail‑driven Procurement Manager to lead sourcing initiatives, strengthen supplier partnerships, and drive KPI‑based performance across our national maintenance network. This role is ideal for a self‑starter who thrives in a fast‑paced environment, collaborates effectively across teams, and consistently delivers high‑quality outcomes.

You will play a critical role in optimizing cost, quality, compliance, and operational readiness, ensuring SFM maintains a competitive edge while supporting essential services nationwide.

Key Responsibilities

The Procurement Manager oversees the full procurement lifecycle — from requisition through delivery — ensuring every transaction aligns with SFM policies, quality standards, and operational readiness requirements. This role leads to strategic sourcing initiatives that strengthen supplier performance, improve cost and quality outcomes, and expand SFM’s nationwide vendor network. The manager conducts high‑impact supplier negotiations, secures competitive terms, and drives continuous improvement through structured supplier performance management.

This position owns core procurement KPIs, including cost savings, cycle‑time reduction, supplier compliance, and readiness metrics, partnering closely with Operations, Finance, and field teams to meet department‑wide targets. Responsibilities include analyzing procurement data, developing actionable insights, supporting leadership reporting, and performing ongoing market research to identify and evaluate new supplier opportunities.

The role also provides urgent and off‑hours procurement support as needed, serves as a designated member of SFM’s snow‑season on‑call team, and coordinates suppliers, materials, and emergency need to ensure uninterrupted service. The Procurement Manager maintains a positive, collaborative presence, supports team training, and assists other divisions to uphold SFM’s culture of operational excellence.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate brings 5+ years of procurement experience, preferably within maintenance or facilities services, with a strong track record of managing high‑volume, nationwide vendor networks. They possess advanced negotiation and contract management skills, deep knowledge of procurement best practices, and proven success in strategic sourcing across multi‑trade environments.

Candidates must demonstrate exceptional analytical ability, sound decision‑making, and meticulous attention to detail, paired with excellent written and verbal communication skills and the ability to turn challenges into actionable solutions. A self‑starter mindset is essential, along with the capability to work independently while supporting team‑wide KPIs and departmental goals.

Technical proficiency with tools such as Smartsheet, Salesforce, MS Office, and other procurement platforms is required. This role also demands strong problem‑solving skills, a commitment to continuous improvement, and the ability to build effective relationships across all levels of the organization. Experience with maintenance vendors, service contracts, and multi‑trade operational environments is strongly preferred.

Why Join SFM?

  • Opportunity to shape procurement strategy across multi‑state operations
  • High‑impact role supporting essential services and emergency readiness
  • Collaborative, supportive team environment
  • Strong focus on innovation, continuous improvement, and operational excellence

raw.title: Director, Product Management (Value Added Solutions)
raw.excerpt: As Director of Product Management, Value Added Solutions, you own the strategy, roadmap, and P&L for NMI's Value Added Solutions business line.
raw.description:
As Director of Product Management, Value Added Solutions, you own the strategy, roadmap, and P&L for NMI's Value Added Solutions business line. Reporting to the Chief Product Officer, you will set direction, lead a small but impactful team of Product Managers and Designers, and stay deeply hands-on: joining customer calls, negotiating with partners, working with engineers to create and deliver a meaningful roadmap, collaborating and advocating with multiple cross-functional teams across NMI, and making the hard product calls when needed.

This is a remote role based in the US.

About NMI

NMI, a global leader in payment technologies, allows software and sales professionals to deliver payment innovations to their clients without having to build payment expertise in house. NMI enables our partners with choice, and challenges the one-size-fits-all approach to payments. You've probably used NMI in the last 24 hours without even realizing it. We're the platform that powers success for innovative tech created by SMBs, entrepreneurs and fintech startups. We're creative problem solvers who help visionaries smash through boundaries and think beyond what's possible so they can think about what's next. But we're not just built for the tech savvy. We democratize the latest payments technology so that everyone can realize the benefits of easy payments across the full spectrum of commerce. Our mission is to use our expertise to enable more payments, in more ways and more places. We provide ISOs, Fintech Innovators and Technologists the freedom to focus on what they do best, liberating them from restricted payment solutions and giving them access to the latest payment technology now and in the future.

How We Work - Our Core Values

  • Be a Good Person, It's Simple. We treat everyone fairly and with respect. We lead with kindness, humility and integrity. We take the time to understand each other and our customers. And we serve with care, because customers are never a transaction, and always our focus
  • Align, Trust & Go. We debate openly, listen carefully and challenge thoughtfully. Once we decide, we move forward together - holding ourselves accountable to our commitments, and focusing on what matters most to our customers. That alignment creates momentum.
  • Raise the Bar. Good enough isn't enough. We stay curious, measure everything, stay honest about progress and keep pushing ourselves to think creatively. We drive change, again and again. And leave things better than we found them. When we raise the bar, our customers feel it too.

About the Team

Value Added Solutions is one of NMI's highest-growth product areas. Our partners want more than payment processing: they want the surrounding capabilities that help their merchants run and grow a business, and they want those capabilities delivered through the platform they already use. That demand is expanding faster than any single team can build against, which makes disciplined choices about what to build, what to buy, and when to partner central to this role.

The Value Added Solutions line spans a portfolio of products, some built in house and some delivered through third parties. You will own that portfolio end to end: which products earn continued investment, which new ones are worth launching, how they reach market through our partner channel, and what each one contributes to the bottom line.

While there are existing products to maintain, this is largely a build role. You will be setting strategy in a space that is moving fast, with real revenue goals and growing partner demand.

You will:

  • Own the product vision, multi-year roadmap, strategy, and P&L for NMI's Value Added Solutions (VAS) product line.
  • Drive business development and growth of the channel: determine whether to invest in existing products or integrate and launch new ones, backed by substantiated business cases with clear revenue targets, margin expectations, and partner adoption metrics.
  • Rank VAS opportunities by upside, effort, and speed to market, and screen each for SMB fit, GTM practicality, and channel enablement.
  • Build the ROI and revenue projections behind every build, buy, or partner decision, and track actuals against them.
  • Work with Sales and Marketing to drive adoption, growth, and customer satisfaction across the portfolio, including cross-sell and upsell into NMI's existing partner base of 6,000+ ISOs and ISVs and the millions of merchant customers they support.
  • Build tight feedback loops with Sales, Account Management, and Support, using their partner relationships and frontline insight to validate ideas early, pilot with the right partners, and adjust quickly after launch.
  • Facilitate partner advisory board sessions for additional insights in coordination with Marketing.
  • Lead your existing and new products across functions including Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Legal, Finance, and Support, and establish the compliance, risk, and operational frameworks each solution needs.
  • Partner with Engineering leadership on architecture, integration approach, and operational readiness for new and existing solutions.
  • Own a repeatable launch playbook that cuts time to market, identifying the efficiencies and automation that standardize how new products roll out.
  • Serve as the key business owner of third-party contracts executed in service of Value Added Solutions, from commercial terms through ongoing performance.
  • Develop a deep understanding of partner and merchant use cases and translate them into a differentiated product strategy.
  • Stay abreast of market trends and customer interests by visiting key customers, attending conferences, participating in webinars, and reading industry material, using those insights to shape competitive positioning, pricing, and roadmap decisions.
  • Become a thought leadership advocate for NMI: participate in podcasts, write blogs and articles, and speak at industry conferences.
  • Participate in planning cadences with Product and Engineering, including ideation, intake, quarterly planning, annual planning, retrospectives, showcases, and hackathons.
  • Build, manage, and develop a team of Product Managers and Designers: set OKRs, maintain growth plans, run performance management, and lead by example in the craft of product management, AI, and payments.
  • Contribute to NMI's product culture by sharing market insights, mentoring PMs across value streams, and participating in hiring and onboarding.
  • Use AI tools actively in your workflow (spec writing, competitive analysis, customer feedback synthesis, discovery acceleration) and show your team how to incorporate AI into their own ways of working.

Minimum Requirements:

  • 8+ years in product management with at least 5 years in payments or financial services, and at least 3 years managing a team of geographically distributed PMs, with a track record of developing talent in a fast-paced, high-performance business unit.
  • Hands-on experience owning a portfolio of products rather than a single feature set, including data-driven decisions to build, buy, partner, or sunset.
  • Experience building prioritization frameworks and ROI-based business cases.
  • Demonstrated track record of building and growing revenue-generating products: defining pricing, owning a product P&L, driving partner GTM execution, and connecting every product decision to revenue impact, partner growth, and customer satisfaction.
  • Experience owning commercial relationships with third-party vendors or technology partners, including contract negotiation and ongoing performance management.
  • Player/coach mentality: you write the strategy doc and still review the acceptance criteria and participate in UAT. You don't disappear into leadership abstraction.
  • Strong commercial instincts: you connect every product decision to revenue impact, partner growth, merchant volume, and customer satisfaction.
  • Deep experience working directly with customers (defining personas, jobs to be done, and feedback loops) and using data-driven insights to identify key performance drivers and inform prioritization.
  • Exceptional execution skills with a bias towards action: you operate in ambiguity, build structure where none exists, and adapt rapidly to shifting priorities.
  • Fluent with AI tools for product work: you use them daily and expect your team to do the same.
  • Exceptional communicator, comfortable presenting a three-year vision to the C-suite, walking a new partner through product details, and representing NMI publicly on a conference stage, all in the same week.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience launching products through an ISO, ISV, or reseller channel.
  • Experience integrating third-party technology into a platform and taking it to market under your own brand.
  • Experience leading a product through a corporate acquisition, including integration strategy, platform consolidation, and team culture alignment.
  • SaaS or B2B embedded finance background.
  • MBA or equivalent experience in high-growth fintech.

Do you feel like you have a slightly out of the ordinary career path or history? We are open to all walks of life and very willing to hear your story. Please don't feel like this should be a barrier to securing a great career at NMI! We appreciate success can come in all shapes and sizes. Fill in the 'Additional Info' box on our application to tell us more about your path.

As well as being a part of something exciting everyday, you will also receive the following benefits:

  • A remote first culture!
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Personal growth and advancement opportunities
  • Flex PTO & dedicated sick time
  • Health, Dental and Vision Insurance
  • Life, ADD, Short-term and Long-term Disability insurance
  • 401k matching up to 4% after two months of service
  • Flexible Spending Account
  • Paid Parental Leave
  • Company volunteer days
  • Employee referral program
  • Bonusly colleague recognition

We believe that having a diverse group of employees strengthens both our work and our workplace. We're focused on making NMI more diverse and welcoming with initiatives like having a dedicated Diversity, Equity & Inclusion action group, diversity goals for hiring, anonymized resume screening, affinity groups such as our Women's network and LGBTQ+ Network, open forums for discussions on diversity and social justice, and measuring inclusion and belonging as part of our regular employee engagement surveys.

Equal Opportunity

NMI is committed to providing equal employment opportunity for all persons regardless of race, color, religion, sex, age, marital status, national origin, sexual orientation or sexual identity, genetic information, citizen status (except those that do not have the legal right to be employed in the United States), disability, military service, service member, veteran status, or any other basis protected by applicable law.

Please be aware that all offers of employment are made subject to receipt of satisfactory background and financial checks.

Attention job applicants: Please note that in compliance with the data protection regulations within your jurisdiction, any personal information submitted with your job application may be collected and used by NMI for the purpose of recruitment and employment-related activities. By submitting your application, you acknowledge and provide explicit consent to the processing of your personal information as described in our privacy policy found on our website. For more information on how we process your information, please read our privacy policy here:

raw.description:
Job Title: Site Navigator I & II - Remote US & Canada

Job Location: Durham

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Job Overview:

Site Navigators play a critical role in the comprehensive coordination of site-level activities throughout the start-up phase of a clinical study and potentially through closeout activities as required. Serving as the single point of contact for investigative sites, this role ensures smooth progression from feasibility and initial outreach through to site activation, extending through the maintenance phase of the study as required. A crucial component in meeting the requirements of the Site Navigator role is ensuring regulatory compliance, robust site management, optimal site support and training, and effective collaboration between the sponsor, CRO, and clinical site staff.

Summary of Responsibilities:

  • Oversight of site level tasks associated with efficient site activation in accordance with ICH/GCP guidelines, local regulations, SOPs and project requirements, including collaboration with project leadership and local monitors to collaboratively achieve project milestones while also ensuring Study Participant rights, wellbeing and safety are protected
  • Identifying potential research sites that align with the study's criteria and assessing their capabilities and resources
  • Conduct initial site outreach, i.e., site engagement, collection of Confidentiality Agreement, and collection of feasibility survey
  • Apply independent judgment and discretion in managing site-level activities, resolving issues, and making decisions that support study timelines and compliance requirements.
  • Remote Pre-Study Visits and follow up documentation, including visit preparation, trip report completion, and other documentation as required to support site selection in line with sponsor, protocol, local and country regulations and requirements
  • Support customization and translation of informed consent forms and patient-facing materials.
  • Collect, track and perform a quality review of all essential documents required for effective and compliant study site activation from site outreach, submissions, greenlight and until site activation. Maintenance and ongoing awareness of site regulatory compliance, supporting annual IRB/Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) renewals, PI changes, and document expirations will be performed as applicable in compliance with local requirements.
  • Actively participate in study team meetings to support study progress, develop and implement action plans for site level risks, underperforming sites, or issues impacting project milestones and escalate issues in a timely manner
  • Support the CRA team in preparing for site initiation visits (SIVs) by coordinating with vendors, supplies teams, and study leads to ensure timely distribution of clinical study supplies, accesses and documents per study team guidance
  • Responsible for submissions to and liaise with applicable IRB/IEC, Third Bodies (if applicable), and Regulatory Authorities by collaborating with Global Regulatory Submissions Lead (GRSL)
  • Perform initial contract and budget negotiations with the sites, as well as amended where applicable.
  • Ensure high quality documents are filed in applicable systems in accordance with SOPs and project requirements and that the Trial Master File (TMF) is updated and audit ready at all times.
  • Track the progress of the start-up process and ensure that the research site meets all requirements and deadlines.
  • Ensure Fortrea is audit ready by completing accurate, timely, and consistent system compliance on an ongoing basis
  • Serve as primary contact for investigative sites and ensure timely delivery in alignment with scope of work/study budget
  • Perform Case Report Form (CRF) review and data validation against source documentation according to protocol and guidelines as applicable in combination with monitoring for site protocol deviations, Serious Adverse Event (SAE) reporting, and all other duties as needed or assigned throughout the course of the study.
  • Perform country and site ICF review/customization, per local requirements
  • All other duties as needed or assigned

Qualifications (Minimum Required):

  • University/College degree (life science preferred), or certification in a related allied health profession from an appropriate accredited institution (e.g., nursing certification, medical or laboratory technology) or 2-3 years' work experience in clinical research, including a working knowledge of the ICH/GCP guidelines and RA, IRB/IEC regulations.
  • Fortrea may consider relevant and equivalent experience in lieu of educational requirements.
  • In lieu of the above requirement, candidates with a High School Diploma or equivalent AND a minimum of 5 years' work experience in clinical research, including a strong working knowledge of the ICH/GCP guidelines and RA, IRB/IEC regulations will be considered.
  • Fluent in local official language and in English, both written and verbal.

Experience (Minimum Required):

  • A scientific degree and/ or clinical expertise is optimal for this role.
  • At least one year of experience in a related field, (e.g., medical, clinical, pharmaceutical, laboratory research, data analysis, data management or technical writing). One year of clinical research is preferred
  • Basic knowledge of ICH/GCP, RA, IRB/IEC, and other applicable regulations/guidelines; familiarity with investigator start-up documents and contract/budgets negotiation process; previous interaction with operational project teams and investigative sites is preferred.
  • Demonstrated understanding of research protocol requirements
  • Effective communication with various stakeholders, including site staff, CRO personnel, and regulatory authorities.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines simultaneously, ensuring that all requirements are met in a timely manner.
  • Understanding of relevant regulations and guidelines related to clinical trials and research.
  • Ability to identify and resolve potential issues that may arise during the start-up process.
  • Ability to negotiate contracts and budgets effectively with research sites.
  • Employees will leverage their existing experience and skills to assume additional responsibilities within the broader role. These will be aligned with operational requirements and internal training, without altering the fundamental nature or classification of the position.

Target Pay Range: Site Navigator I: $58,000-60,000K USD ; Site Navigator II: $68,000-78,000K

Physical Demands / Work Environment:

  • Remote-based work required with possible office presence depending on location
  • Travel requirements: Limited to training only

Work Environment:

  • Work is performed in an office environment with exposure to electrical office equipment.
  • Frequent travel to clients/ site locations with occasional travel both domestic and international.

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to sit for extended periods and operate a vehicle safely.
  • Repetitive hand movement of both hands with the ability to make fast, simple, repeated movements of the fingers, hands, and wrists.
  • Occasional crouching, stooping, with frequent bending and twisting of upper body and neck.
  • Ability to access and use a variety of computer software developed both in-house and off-the-shelf.
  • Light to moderate lifting and carrying (or otherwise moves) objects including luggage and laptop computer with a maximum lift of 15-20 lbs.
  • Regular and consistent attendance.
  • Varied hours may be required.

Please note that we currently do not have any positions open; however, if you would like to be considered for future opportunities, please submit your application materials for the Research Consultant position in the San Francisco Bay Area or the greater Los Angeles region. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and our team will be in touch if an opportunity becomes available.

Who We Are

Engage R+D is a strategic learning and evaluation firm with a passionate and energetic team of diverse professionals who believe in the power of evaluation and research to advance equity and fuel social change. We bring together people, data, and ideas in creative ways to inform strategy and drive results in the social sector. We approach our work with intellectual curiosity, a sense of humility, and grounding in the communities that are ultimately impacted by what we do. Through a collaborative team-based approach, we engage stakeholders in collective problem-solving and strive to draw upon our diverse perspectives and strengths. We believe in the importance of a collaborative and intellectually stimulating environment that supports organizational learning and opportunities to strengthen our practice and advance the field. We seek to create the conditions and space for teams to do their best work. We offer competitive compensation packages, including paid time off and benefits, as well as professional development opportunities and flexible work arrangements. Engage R+D is a California-based virtual consulting firm, and team members typically work from home-based offices and co-working spaces.

Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree (i.e., Master’s degree or higher) in social or behavioral science, public policy, or related area
  • 5+ years of experience applying research, planning, evaluation, and community engagement skills, ideally within a consulting environment
  • Commitment to center and advance equity in our evaluative practice
  • Experience managing projects and implementing multi-faceted work for philanthropic, non-profit, and/or government entities
  • Ability to navigate change, ambiguity, and complex projects
  • Comfort working remotely
  • Fluency in other languages, particularly Spanish, is a plus!

Who You Are

Engage R+D seeks curious and creative people passionate about using data and evaluation to improve results and drive social change. You are an experienced evaluator with fluency in qualitative and quantitative methods, strong people skills, and the ability to engage diverse groups of people in learning and evaluation. You bring outstanding written and verbal communication skills and can translate findings into actionable plans and practitioner-friendly reports. You enjoy working across multiple content areas and tapping into new and innovative approaches.

Evaluation in real-world settings can be messy, but you are comfortable with ambiguity and navigating complex situations. You’re able to focus on the big picture while managing the details and identifying solutions. You have strong listening skills and bring cultural humility to the work, seeking to understand and bridge the needs and experiences of diverse stakeholders. You actively demonstrate commitment to equity and inclusion by showing respect, humility, and cultural sensitivity in all aspects of your work and interactions. You are adept at working with diverse communities and are able to facilitate inclusive discussions with a range of stakeholders, from community residents and non-profit leaders to foundation and public sector staff. You thrive in an entrepreneurial and team-driven environment. Finally, you’re enthusiastic about contributing to a young and innovative organization.

What You’ll Do at Engage R+D

Research Consultants design, manage and execute multi-faceted projects for philanthropic, non-profit, and government clients. Research Consultants are responsible for client-facing work that spans the full life cycle of the project, from scoping, design, data collection, and analysis to reporting and facilitating learning sessions with clients and community stakeholders. We value contributions from all team members to strengthen internal operations, infrastructure, and organizational well-being.

Essential Functions & Duties

As a project manager, you’ll work closely with project directors and team members to co-design and implement work plans, collect and analyze data (qualitative and quantitative), and support the production of high-quality, actionable products. You’ll also be actively involved in efforts to facilitate and engage diverse stakeholders in co-creation, sensemaking, and shared learning.
  • Organizational contributions: You’ll have ample opportunities to contribute to our organizational development and success by participating in team retreats and workgroups focused on business development, organizational learning, communications, field building, and strengthening internal infrastructure. If you’re seeking opportunities to shape organizational culture and explore innovative approaches with like-minded colleagues, this is the place for you!

Compensation

We offer a competitive compensation package and create a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. The starting salary range for this position is $80,000 - $100,000, and benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • Health insurance for employees with a range of provider options and tiers, as well as full dental and vision
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer contribution
  • Paid Time Off (PTO) of six weeks during the first year (inclusive of sick, federal holidays, and vacation time)
  • Professional development funds ($1,000 annually)
  • Wellness benefits include a monthly stipend for a gym membership or wellness activities
  • Equipment and monthly phone stipend for virtual home office

How to Apply

If you are interested in being considered for future opportunities to join our team, please submit a resume and cover letter via this link: Apply Here. In your cover letter, please address the following five questions:

  • What makes you interested in Engage R+D?
  • What aspects of your previous experience have prepared you for a position with us?
  • What does it mean for you to have a commitment to equity, and how would you see yourself demonstrating it at Engage R+D?
  • What skills could you bring to Engage R+D that may not be apparent from looking at your resume or career history?

Engage R+D is an Equal Opportunity organization with a strong commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion. We welcome applications from all and strongly encourage individuals underrepresented in the workforce to apply.

raw.excerpt: Cross-industry, insurance-first | Global remit | Americas-based, remote | Reports to the Chief Commercial Officer Who we areAdlib is the AI Production Layer for regulated industries.
raw.description:
Cross-industry, insurance-first | Global remit | Americas-based, remote | Reports to the Chief Commercial Officer

Who we are

Adlib is the AI Production Layer for regulated industries. We turn complex, unstructured documents into governed, validated, AI-ready data so enterprises can make defensible decisions without rebuilding their stack. Customers see 60% fewer exceptions, 50% faster cycle times and 70% less manual handling.

On top of that trusted data layer sits our agentic intake capability. Agents read the packet, decide what it is, apply the customer’s rules, route the exception and trigger the next action. The document layer establishes trust in the data. The agentic layer acts on it.

For insurance carriers that means agentic intake across FNOL packets, police reports, medical records, adjuster notes, loss runs, submissions and endorsements. We are model-agnostic and system-agnostic by design, sitting in front of Guidewire, Duck Creek, Sapiens and Majesco rather than replacing any of it. We serve life sciences, insurance and public sector customers, and we are backed by Diversis Capital.

The role

This is not a standard VP of Sales job. Insurance is our core growth driver and this role goes deepest there, but it carries the whole company number across life sciences, public sector and OEM as well, worldwide. It also has to absorb sellers and systems from an acquisition, and leave the sales function in a state that stands up to institutional scrutiny.

You will inherit a small, capable team and an open field. We are blending a startup mentality with an established business, so you can innovate faster while deploying proven sales tactics and processes that work. You are building the machine: territory and quota design, capacity planning, methodology, deal inspection, and a forecast the Board can rely on. You report to the Chief Commercial Officer and sit on the commercial leadership team.

You will also sell. At our current team size this is a working leadership role, and you will personally lead the largest opportunities in your first two quarters.

The details

Role

Vice President of Sales

Reports to

Chief Commercial Officer

Scope

All new ARR worldwide, cross-industry, with an insurance-first focus

Team

Matrixed leadership with line-of-business General Managers (GMs) of the quota-carrying sales team, scaling with the plan

Location

Remote, based in the Americas. Global remit, with travel of approximately 30%.

Base salary

$175,000 to $200,000 USD

On-target earnings

$350,000 to $400,000 USD (50/50 base and variable, with accelerators above plan)

Equity

Participation in the management incentive plan, with change-of-control treatment

What you will own

  • The number. Carry and deliver the company new ARR number worldwide, across all industries, direct and partner-influenced. You are based in the Americas and the remit is global, including EMEA.
  • Team build. Recruit, ramp and coach the quota-carrying team. Expect to spend a meaningful share of your time on hiring. The team you build in your first six months is what shows up in bookings in your second year.
  • Capacity and quota. Own territory design, quota assignment, and the sales capacity model. Quota is derived from rep productivity and carries deliberate over-assignment, not calculated backwards from the target.
  • Forecast integrity. Own a weekly forecast with defined stage exit criteria and conversion rates derived from actual closed-deal history. Forecast means high confidence, not hope.
  • Insurance leadership. Go deepest in insurance. Own the executive relationships at target carriers, MGAs, TPAs and brokers, and make sure our claims and underwriting story lands with operators, not just IT.

  • Hold the differentiation line. Our biggest competitive risk is being boxed as another OCR or IDP tool by buyers who have been pitched by every extraction vendor and are now hearing agentic AI from their core platform vendor as well.
  • Acquisition integration. Bring the acquired selling team onto one CRM, one pipeline, one forecast and one comp philosophy. Retain the sellers worth retaining, resolve account conflict, and deliver the cross-sell the acquisition was underwritten on.
  • Cross-functional partnership. Partner with the Industry General Managers on vertical strategy and named accounts, with Marketing on pipeline coverage, with Strategic Partnerships on partner-sourced opportunities, and with Revenue Operations on quota, comp mechanics and reporting.
  • Institutional readiness. Keep the sales function audit-ready. Cohort retention, quota attainment distribution, pipeline quality, win-loss, sales cycle by segment and forecast accuracy history should be current at all times, not reconstructed under deadline.

What you bring

  • Scale experience. You have taken B2B software businesses from $2M to $50M or more in ARR in a sales leadership seat. You can speak precisely to ARR, seller count and per-rep productivity at the start and the end.
  • Insurance depth. You have sold into insurance carriers, MGAs, TPAs, brokers or reinsurers and can hold a conversation with a Chief Claims Officer or Chief Underwriting Officer on their terms. You understand the claims and submission lifecycle, loss ratio and expense ratio, cycle time, leakage and straight-through processing. You know your way around Guidewire, Duck Creek and the wider core and content stack, and around ACORD and ISO forms, NAIC and state DOI expectations.
  • Cross-industry range. You have carried a number across two or more unrelated verticals at the same time. You know how to keep a small team focused without letting one vertical starve the others.
  • Global remit. You have led sellers or carried a number across more than one region, including Europe. You know how deal cycles, buying norms and employment practice differ outside North America, and you can run a team you do not sit beside.
  • A team you built. You have personally recruited and ramped five to eight quota carriers. You can name them and say where they are now.
  • Operating rigor. You build quota from steady-state rep productivity, plan for ramp, and can explain your capacity model on a whiteboard. You track attainment as a distribution, not an average.
  • Acquisition integration. You have merged two selling teams after an acquisition. You have made the single versus dual go-to-market call, harmonized comp and territories without losing the people who mattered, and consolidated onto one pipeline.
  • Exit experience. You have owned the sales side of a sale process or major diligence. You know what a buyer or banker asks the sales organization for, and what breaks when the data does not hold up.
  • Enterprise and regulated selling. You are credible on AI without overselling it. You sell business outcomes and defensible data, not model hype.
  • A working leader. You are still close enough to the work to run a deal yourself, and you want to be. You take coaching as readily as you give it.

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical experience.

Nice to have

  • Experience in a private equity backed company with a defined growth mandate and reporting cadence.
  • Relationships in the insurance systems integrator ecosystem, including Guidewire and Duck Creek implementation partners.
  • Experience selling AI, intelligent document processing or data platform solutions into regulated industries.
  • Life sciences or public sector selling experience alongside insurance.
  • Experience selling in Canada and Latin America as well as the United States.

What is in it for you

This is a rare shape of role: enough scale that the fundamentals exist, enough whitespace that you will build most of what matters, and a clear horizon to build toward. You will have direct access to the CEO and the Board, and your work will be visible in every conversation about the company’s value.

Adlib’s headquarters are in Burlington, Ontario. This role is remote and based in the Americas, with a global remit. We care about employee health and wellness and build programs around personal and professional satisfaction. Our employee programs and benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • Wellness and lifestyle spending account
  • RRSP or 401(k) matching
  • No limit vacation
  • Extended maternity and paternity leave
  • Employee assistance programs, and much more

To learn more about this role, please express your interest here, or follow us on LinkedIn for future opportunities.

Adlib seeks to inspire and nurture the human spirit. We understand that each person brings a distinct life experience to the table. Embracing diversity not only enhances our work culture, it drives business success. Adlib encourages applications from everybody, regardless of race, colour, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

Salary: $175,000-200,000 USD Annually + Commission

Key Responsibilities

The Procurement Manager oversees the full procurement lifecycle — from requisition through delivery — ensuring every transaction aligns with SFM policies, quality standards, and operational readiness requirements. This role leads to strategic sourcing initiatives that strengthen supplier performance, improve cost and quality outcomes, and expand SFM’s nationwide vendor network. raw.excerpt: As Director of Product Management, Value Added Solutions, you own the strategy, roadmap, and P&L for NMI's Value Added Solutions business line.
raw.description:
As Director of Product Management, Value Added Solutions, you own the strategy, roadmap, and P&L for NMI's Value Added Solutions business line. Reporting to the Chief Product Officer, you will set direction, lead a small but impactful team of Product Managers and Designers, and stay deeply hands-on: joining customer calls, negotiating with partners, working with engineers to create and deliver a meaningful roadmap, collaborating and advocating with multiple cross-functional teams across NMI, and making the hard product calls when needed.

This is a remote role based in the US.

About NMI

NMI, a global leader in payment technologies, allows software and sales professionals to deliver payment innovations to their clients without having to build payment expertise in house. NMI enables our partners with choice, and challenges the one-size-fits-all approach to payments. You've probably used NMI in the last 24 hours without even realizing it. We're the platform that powers success for innovative tech created by SMBs, entrepreneurs and fintech startups. We're creative problem solvers who help visionaries smash through boundaries and think beyond what's possible so they can think about what's next. But we're not just built for the tech savvy. We democratize the latest payments technology so that everyone can realize the benefits of easy payments across the full spectrum of commerce. Our mission is to use our expertise to enable more payments, in more ways and more places. We provide ISOs, Fintech Innovators and Technologists the freedom to focus on what they do best, liberating them from restricted payment solutions and giving them access to the latest payment technology now and in the future.

How We Work - Our Core Values

  • Be a Good Person, It's Simple. We treat everyone fairly and with respect. We lead with kindness, humility and integrity. We take the time to understand each other and our customers. And we serve with care, because customers are never a transaction, and always our focus
  • Align, Trust & Go. We debate openly, listen carefully and challenge thoughtfully. Once we decide, we move forward together - holding ourselves accountable to our commitments, and focusing on what matters most to our customers. That alignment creates momentum.
  • Raise the Bar. Good enough isn't enough. We stay curious, measure everything, stay honest about progress and keep pushing ourselves to think creatively. We drive change, again and again. And leave things better than we found them. When we raise the bar, our customers feel it too.

About the Team

Value Added Solutions is one of NMI's highest-growth product areas. Our partners want more than payment processing: they want the surrounding capabilities that help their merchants run and grow a business, and they want those capabilities delivered through the platform they already use. That demand is expanding faster than any single team can build against, which makes disciplined choices about what to build, what to buy, and when to partner central to this role.

The Value Added Solutions line spans a portfolio of products, some built in house and some delivered through third parties. You will own that portfolio end to end: which products earn continued investment, which new ones are worth launching, how they reach market through our partner channel, and what each one contributes to the bottom line.

While there are existing products to maintain, this is largely a build role. You will be setting strategy in a space that is moving fast, with real revenue goals and growing partner demand.

You will:

  • Own the product vision, multi-year roadmap, strategy, and P&L for NMI's Value Added Solutions (VAS) product line.
  • Drive business development and growth of the channel: determine whether to invest in existing products or integrate and launch new ones, backed by substantiated business cases with clear revenue targets, margin expectations, and partner adoption metrics.
  • Rank VAS opportunities by upside, effort, and speed to market, and screen each for SMB fit, GTM practicality, and channel enablement.
  • Build the ROI and revenue projections behind every build, buy, or partner decision, and track actuals against them.
  • Work with Sales and Marketing to drive adoption, growth, and customer satisfaction across the portfolio, including cross-sell and upsell into NMI's existing partner base of 6,000+ ISOs and ISVs and the millions of merchant customers they support.
  • Build tight feedback loops with Sales, Account Management, and Support, using their partner relationships and frontline insight to validate ideas early, pilot with the right partners, and adjust quickly after launch.
  • Facilitate partner advisory board sessions for additional insights in coordination with Marketing.
  • Lead your existing and new products across functions including Sales, Marketing, Engineering, Legal, Finance, and Support, and establish the compliance, risk, and operational frameworks each solution needs.
  • Partner with Engineering leadership on architecture, integration approach, and operational readiness for new and existing solutions.
  • Own a repeatable launch playbook that cuts time to market, identifying the efficiencies and automation that standardize how new products roll out.
  • Serve as the key business owner of third-party contracts executed in service of Value Added Solutions, from commercial terms through ongoing performance.
  • Develop a deep understanding of partner and merchant use cases and translate them into a differentiated product strategy.
  • Stay abreast of market trends and customer interests by visiting key customers, attending conferences, participating in webinars, and reading industry material, using those insights to shape competitive positioning, pricing, and roadmap decisions.
  • Become a thought leadership advocate for NMI: participate in podcasts, write blogs and articles, and speak at industry conferences.
  • Participate in planning cadences with Product and Engineering, including ideation, intake, quarterly planning, annual planning, retrospectives, showcases, and hackathons.
  • Build, manage, and develop a team of Product Managers and Designers: set OKRs, maintain growth plans, run performance management, and lead by example in the craft of product management, AI, and payments.
  • Contribute to NMI's product culture by sharing market insights, mentoring PMs across value streams, and participating in hiring and onboarding.
  • Use AI tools actively in your workflow (spec writing, competitive analysis, customer feedback synthesis, discovery acceleration) and show your team how to incorporate AI into their own ways of working.

Minimum Requirements:

  • 8+ years in product management with at least 5 years in payments or financial services, and at least 3 years managing a team of geographically distributed PMs, with a track record of developing talent in a fast-paced, high-performance business unit.
  • Hands-on experience owning a portfolio of products rather than a single feature set, including data-driven decisions to build, buy, partner, or sunset.
  • Experience building prioritization frameworks and ROI-based business cases.
  • Demonstrated track record of building and growing revenue-generating products: defining pricing, owning a product P&L, driving partner GTM execution, and connecting every product decision to revenue impact, partner growth, and customer satisfaction.
  • Experience owning commercial relationships with third-party vendors or technology partners, including contract negotiation and ongoing performance management.
  • Player/coach mentality: you write the strategy doc and still review the acceptance criteria and participate in UAT. You don't disappear into leadership abstraction.
  • Strong commercial instincts: you connect every product decision to revenue impact, partner growth, merchant volume, and customer satisfaction.
  • Deep experience working directly with customers (defining personas, jobs to be done, and feedback loops) and using data-driven insights to identify key performance drivers and inform prioritization.
  • Exceptional execution skills with a bias towards action: you operate in ambiguity, build structure where none exists, and adapt rapidly to shifting priorities.
  • Fluent with AI tools for product work: you use them daily and expect your team to do the same.
  • Exceptional communicator, comfortable presenting a three-year vision to the C-suite, walking a new partner through product details, and representing NMI publicly on a conference stage, all in the same week.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience launching products through an ISO, ISV, or reseller channel.
  • Experience integrating third-party technology into a platform and taking it to market under your own brand.
  • Experience leading a product through a corporate acquisition, including integration strategy, platform consolidation, and team culture alignment.
  • SaaS or B2B embedded finance background.
  • MBA or equivalent experience in high-growth fintech.

Do you feel like you have a slightly out of the ordinary career path or history? We are open to all walks of life and very willing to hear your story. Please don't feel like this should be a barrier to securing a great career at NMI! We appreciate success can come in all shapes and sizes. Fill in the 'Additional Info' box on our application to tell us more about your path.

As well as being a part of something exciting everyday, you will also receive the following benefits:

  • A remote first culture!
  • Competitive compensation and benefits
  • Personal growth and advancement opportunities
  • Flex PTO & dedicated sick time
  • Health, Dental and Vision Insurance
  • Life, ADD, Short-term and Long-term Disability insurance

raw.description:
Job Title: Site Navigator I & II - Remote US & Canada

Job Location: Durham

Job Location Type: Remote

Job Contract Type: Full-time

Job Seniority Level:

Job Overview:

Site Navigators play a critical role in the comprehensive coordination of site-level activities throughout the start-up phase of a clinical study and potentially through closeout activities as required. Serving as the single point of contact for investigative sites, this role ensures smooth progression from feasibility and initial outreach through to site activation, extending through the maintenance phase of the study as required. A crucial component in meeting the requirements of the Site Navigator role is ensuring regulatory compliance, robust site management, optimal site support and training, and effective collaboration between the sponsor, CRO, and clinical site staff.

Summary of Responsibilities:

  • Oversight of site level tasks associated with efficient site activation in accordance with ICH/GCP guidelines, local regulations, SOPs and project requirements, including collaboration with project leadership and local monitors to collaboratively achieve project milestones while also ensuring Study Participant rights, wellbeing and safety are protected
  • Identifying potential research sites that align with the study's criteria and assessing their capabilities and resources
  • Conduct initial site outreach, i.e., site engagement, collection of Confidentiality Agreement, and collection of feasibility survey
  • Apply independent judgment and discretion in managing site-level activities, resolving issues, and making decisions that support study timelines and compliance requirements.
  • Remote Pre-Study Visits and follow up documentation, including visit preparation, trip report completion, and other documentation as required to support site selection in line with sponsor, protocol, local and country regulations and requirements
  • Support customization and translation of informed consent forms and patient-facing materials.
  • Collect, track and perform a quality review of all essential documents required for effective and compliant study site activation from site outreach, submissions, greenlight and until site activation. Maintenance and ongoing awareness of site regulatory compliance, supporting annual IRB/Independent Ethics Committee (IEC) renewals, PI changes, and document expirations will be performed as applicable in compliance with local requirements.
  • Actively participate in study team meetings to support study progress, develop and implement action plans for site level risks, underperforming sites, or issues impacting project milestones and escalate issues in a timely manner
  • Support the CRA team in preparing for site initiation visits (SIVs) by coordinating with vendors, supplies teams, and study leads to ensure timely distribution of clinical study supplies, accesses and documents per study team guidance
  • Responsible for submissions to and liaise with applicable IRB/IEC, Third Bodies (if applicable), and Regulatory Authorities by collaborating with Global Regulatory Submissions Lead (GRSL)
  • Perform initial contract and budget negotiations with the sites, as well as amended where applicable.
  • Ensure high quality documents are filed in applicable systems in accordance with SOPs and project requirements and that the Trial Master File (TMF) is updated and audit ready at all times.
  • Track the progress of the start-up process and ensure that the research site meets all requirements and deadlines.
  • Ensure Fortrea is audit ready by completing accurate, timely, and consistent system compliance on an ongoing basis
  • Serve as primary contact for investigative sites and ensure timely delivery in alignment with scope of work/study budget
  • Perform Case Report Form (CRF) review and data validation against source documentation according to protocol and guidelines as applicable in combination with monitoring for site protocol deviations, Serious Adverse Event (SAE) reporting, and all other duties as needed or assigned throughout the course of the study.
  • Perform country and site ICF review/customization, per local requirements
  • All other duties as needed or assigned

Qualifications (Minimum Required):

  • University/College degree (life science preferred), or certification in a related allied health profession from an appropriate accredited institution (e.g., nursing certification, medical or laboratory technology) or 2-3 years' work experience in clinical research, including a working knowledge of the ICH/GCP guidelines and RA, IRB/IEC regulations.
  • Fortrea may consider relevant and equivalent experience in lieu of educational requirements.
  • In lieu of the above requirement, candidates with a High School Diploma or equivalent AND a minimum of 5 years' work experience in clinical research, including a strong working knowledge of the ICH/GCP guidelines and RA, IRB/IEC regulations will be considered.
  • Fluent in local official language and in English, both written and verbal.

Experience (Minimum Required):

  • A scientific degree and/ or clinical expertise is optimal for this role.
  • At least one year of experience in a related field, (e.g., medical, clinical, pharmaceutical, laboratory research, data analysis, data management or technical writing). One year of clinical research is preferred
  • Basic knowledge of ICH/GCP, RA, IRB/IEC, and other applicable regulations/guidelines; familiarity with investigator start-up documents and contract/budgets negotiation process; previous interaction with operational project teams and investigative sites is preferred.
  • Demonstrated understanding of research protocol requirements
  • Effective communication with various stakeholders, including site staff, CRO personnel, and regulatory authorities.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines simultaneously, ensuring that all requirements are met in a timely manner.
  • Understanding of relevant regulations and guidelines related to clinical trials and research.
  • Ability to identify and resolve potential issues that may arise during the start-up process.
  • Ability to negotiate contracts and budgets effectively with research sites.
  • Employees will leverage their existing experience and skills to assume additional responsibilities within the broader role. These will be aligned with operational requirements and internal training, without altering the fundamental nature or classification of the position.

Target Pay Range: Site Navigator I: $58,000-60,000K USD ; Site Navigator II: $68,000-78,000K

Physical Demands / Work Environment:

  • Remote-based work required with possible office presence depending on location
  • Travel requirements: Limited to training only

Work Environment:

  • Work is performed in an office environment with exposure to electrical office equipment.
  • Frequent travel to clients/ site locations with occasional travel both domestic and international.

Physical Requirements:

  • Ability to sit for extended periods and operate a vehicle safely.
  • Repetitive hand movement of both hands with the ability to make fast, simple, repeated movements of the fingers, hands, and wrists.
  • Occasional crouching, stooping, with frequent bending and twisting of upper body and neck.
  • Ability to access and use a variety of computer software developed both in-house and off-the-shelf.
  • Light to moderate lifting and carrying (or otherwise moves) objects including luggage and laptop computer with a maximum lift of 15-20 lbs.
  • Regular and consistent attendance.
  • Varied hours may be required.

Please note that we currently do not have any positions open; however, if you would like to be considered for future opportunities, please submit your application materials for the Research Consultant position in the San Francisco Bay Area or the greater Los Angeles region. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and our team will be in touch if an opportunity becomes available.

Who We Are

Engage R+D is a strategic learning and evaluation firm with a passionate and energetic team of diverse professionals who believe in the power of evaluation and research to advance equity and fuel social change. We bring together people, data, and ideas in creative ways to inform strategy and drive results in the social sector. We approach our work with intellectual curiosity, a sense of humility, and grounding in the communities that are ultimately impacted by what we do. Through a collaborative team-based approach, we engage stakeholders in collective problem-solving and strive to draw upon our diverse perspectives and strengths. We believe in the importance of a collaborative and intellectually stimulating environment that supports organizational learning and opportunities to strengthen our practice and advance the field. We seek to create the conditions and space for teams to do their best work. We offer competitive compensation packages, including paid time off and benefits, as well as professional development opportunities and flexible work arrangements. Engage R+D is a California-based virtual consulting firm, and team members typically work from home-based offices and co-working spaces.

Qualifications:

  • Advanced degree (i.e., Master’s degree or higher) in social or behavioral science, public policy, or related area
  • 5+ years of experience applying research, planning, evaluation, and community engagement skills, ideally within a consulting environment
  • Commitment to center and advance equity in our evaluative practice
  • Experience managing projects and implementing multi-faceted work for philanthropic, non-profit, and/or government entities
  • Ability to navigate change, ambiguity, and complex projects
  • Comfort working remotely
  • Fluency in other languages, particularly Spanish, is a plus!

Who You Are

Engage R+D seeks curious and creative people passionate about using data and evaluation to improve results and drive social change. You are an experienced evaluator with fluency in qualitative and quantitative methods, strong people skills, and the ability to engage diverse groups of people in learning and evaluation. You bring outstanding written and verbal communication skills and can translate findings into actionable plans and practitioner-friendly reports. You enjoy working across multiple content areas and tapping into new and innovative approaches.

Evaluation in real-world settings can be messy, but you are comfortable with ambiguity and navigating complex situations. You’re able to focus on the big picture while managing the details and identifying solutions. You have strong listening skills and bring cultural humility to the work, seeking to understand and bridge the needs and experiences of diverse stakeholders. You actively demonstrate commitment to equity and inclusion by showing respect, humility, and cultural sensitivity in all aspects of your work and interactions. You are adept at working with diverse communities and are able to facilitate inclusive discussions with a range of stakeholders, from community residents and non-profit leaders to foundation and public sector staff. You thrive in an entrepreneurial and team-driven environment. Finally, you’re enthusiastic about contributing to a young and innovative organization.

What You’ll Do at Engage R+D

Research Consultants design, manage and execute multi-faceted projects for philanthropic, non-profit, and government clients. Research Consultants are responsible for client-facing work that spans the full life cycle of the project, from scoping, design, data collection, and analysis to reporting and facilitating learning sessions with clients and community stakeholders. We value contributions from all team members to strengthen internal operations, infrastructure, and organizational well-being.

Essential Functions & Duties

  • Project management and research support: As a core team member, you’ll serve on multiple project teams, playing various roles from analyst and learning partner to project manager or lead on streams of work. As a project manager, you’ll work closely with project directors and team members to co-design and implement work plans, collect and analyze data (qualitative and quantitative), and support the production of high-quality, actionable products. You’ll also be actively involved in efforts to facilitate and engage diverse stakeholders in co-creation, sensemaking, and shared learning.
  • Organizational contributions: You’ll have ample opportunities to contribute to our organizational development and success by participating in team retreats and workgroups focused on business development, organizational learning, communications, field building, and strengthening internal infrastructure. If you’re seeking opportunities to shape organizational culture and explore innovative approaches with like-minded colleagues, this is the place for you!

Compensation

We offer a competitive compensation package and create a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive. The starting salary range for this position is $80,000 - $100,000, and benefits include, but are not limited to:

  • Health insurance for employees with a range of provider options and tiers, as well as full dental and vision
  • 401(k) retirement plan with employer contribution
  • Paid Time Off (PTO) of six weeks during the first year (inclusive of sick, federal holidays, and vacation time)
  • Professional development funds ($1,000 annually)
  • Wellness benefits include a monthly stipend for a gym membership or wellness activities
  • Equipment and monthly phone stipend for virtual home office

How to Apply

If you are interested in being considered for future opportunities to join our team, please submit a resume and cover letter via this link: Apply Here. In your cover letter, please address the following five questions:

  • What makes you interested in Engage R+D?
  • What aspects of your previous experience have prepared you for a position with us?
  • What does it mean for you to have a commitment to equity, and how would you see yourself demonstrating it at Engage R+D?
  • What skills could you bring to Engage R+D that may not be apparent from looking at your resume or career history?
  • How did you hear about Engage R+D?

Engage R+D is an Equal Opportunity organization with a strong commitment to equity, diversity, and inclusion. We welcome applications from all and strongly encourage individuals underrepresented in the workforce to apply.

Salary: $80,000 - $100,000
